questions.q: Per this lesson, what does it mean if you can't point to a specific lesson/artifact for one of the 10 Definition of Done requirements?
options: It doesn't matter as long as the demo looks good
It means the requirement was optional all along
That requirement isn't actually done -- it's a gap this retrospective is meant to surface before Chapter 5's presentation
It means the requirement was automatically satisfied by another one
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit: a requirement you can't point to a specific lesson for isn't actually done, and the retrospective exists to catch that before the presentation, not during it.

questions.q: What specific finding from Lesson 20 does this lesson cite as worth naming honestly in the retrospective?
options: That WarrantyClaimTriggerHandler's original design genuinely broke at bulk volume and needed a refactor
That the Flow from Lesson 6 was never built
That the REST integration from Lesson 14 was abandoned
That the security model from Lesson 4 was skipped entirely
questions.explain: The lesson calls out the real governor-limit bug found and fixed during performance testing as an example of honest retrospective content, rather than pretending the first version was always correct.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what distinguishes technical debt from a silent shortcut?
options: Technical debt is always a bug; a silent shortcut is always intentional
Technical debt is a deliberate, documented simplification with a stated reason; a silent shortcut is unnamed and easily forgotten
There is no real difference between the two
Technical debt only applies to Apex code, never to Flow
questions.explain: The lesson defines technical debt as a deliberate, documented gap with a reason for the simplification -- naming it explicitly is what separates it from an unremembered silent shortcut.

questions.q: Which of these is named in this lesson as a piece of technical debt this platform knowingly carries?
options: The Case to Installation Job Flow doesn't exist at all
Warranty_Claim__c has no fields at all
No Apex tests were written for any class
The Assign Technician subflow uses simple least-loaded assignment without accounting for technician certification by appliance category
questions.explain: The lesson names the simplified least-loaded technician assignment, StaleInstallationJobBatch's unfinished notification in finish(), and the single-claim-per-callout integration design as explicit technical debt.

questions.q: How does this lesson distinguish the retrospective from Chapter 5's demo and presentation?
options: The retrospective is an honest internal self-assessment for the team; the presentation is a curated, external-facing walkthrough of the platform's strengths
They are identical documents serving the same audience
The retrospective is given live; the presentation is written down
The presentation covers technical debt in full detail; the retrospective does not
questions.explain: The retrospective is internal and honest, including caveats and debt; the presentation is external-facing and curated to show strengths clearly -- both necessary, but serving different purposes.
